title: Rugelach with Walnuts and Cinnamon
summary: Flaky cream cheese pastry rolled around an apricot, walnut and cinnamon filling, baked into golden crescents.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: full-fat cream cheese, cool but not fridge-hard
fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

ingredients.note: beaten with 1 tbsp water, for glazing

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Stir the apricot jam until smooth, then set aside the cinnamon sugar, chopped walnuts and raisins separately, ready to scatter over the dough. Having everything prepared before you start rolling makes the assembly step quick, which matters once the dough is out of the fridge and starting to soften. The jam acts as the glue that holds the nuts and raisins in place.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Beat or pulse the cream cheese, butter, sugar and salt together until smooth, then add the flour and mix just until a soft dough forms. There's no water in this dough at all — the moisture in the cream cheese is what makes the pastry so tender and flaky once baked. Stop mixing as soon as the dough comes together, since overworking it develops too much gluten.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Divide the dough into four, shape each piece into a flat disc, wrap, and chill for at least 2 hours, up to 2 days. This long chill firms the butter and cream cheese back up, which is essential for rolling the dough thinly without it tearing or sticking. Dough that hasn't chilled long enough will feel greasy and hard to work with.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before you start baking, with a shelf in the middle. Line two large metal trays with baking paper while it heats. Starting the bake in a fully heated oven helps the pastry layers set and puff before the filling has a chance to leak out.

steps.title: Roll and fill
steps.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll one disc into a 23 cm round, about 3 mm thick — if it cracks as you roll, let it rest for 5 minutes to relax before continuing. Spread a quarter of the jam over the round to within 1 cm of the edge, then scatter over the cinnamon sugar, walnuts and raisins, pressing lightly so they stick. Leaving that border free of filling stops it squeezing out of the edges as you roll each piece up.

steps.title: Cut and roll into crescents
steps.text: Cut the round into 12 wedges, then roll each one up from the wide end to the point. Set the rolled pieces point-side down, spaced 3 cm apart, on the lined trays. Rolling from the wide end naturally tucks the point underneath, which helps the crescents hold their shape in the oven.

steps.title: Chill the shaped pastries
steps.text: Chill the shaped rugelach for 15-20 minutes before baking. This short second chill firms the butter in the dough one more time, so the layers hold their shape and don't collapse flat as soon as they hit the oven's heat. Use this time to repeat the rolling and filling with the remaining discs.

steps.title: Glaze and bake
steps.text: Brush the chilled pastries with the egg wash and sprinkle with sugar, then bake for 20-25 minutes, until deep golden brown all over. Deep colour matters here: pastries that come out pale can taste raw and floury rather than properly baked through. The egg wash is what gives the crescents their shiny, golden-brown finish.

steps.title: Cool quickly
steps.text: Leave the rugelach on the tray for just 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack. Moving them promptly stops any filling that's leaked out from setting hard and gluing the pastries to the tray. Makes 48 rugelach.

tips: Chill the dough for the full 2 hours minimum — a common shortcut that leaves the dough too soft to roll thinly without tearing.
Leave a clear 1 cm border free of filling around the edge of each round, or it will squeeze out and burn onto the tray as the rugelach roll up.
Bake until deep golden brown rather than just lightly coloured — pale rugelach taste undercooked and floury in the middle.
Move the baked pastries off the tray within 5 minutes, since any leaked filling sets hard fast and can stick them in place.
If the dough cracks while rolling, don't force it — let it rest for 5 minutes to relax before continuing.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days. Both baked and unbaked shaped rugelach freeze well for up to 3 months; bake unbaked ones straight from frozen, adding 5 minutes to the time.
